title: Efficient Machines in Motion

competencies.text: Design, construct, and test a simple or compound machine.
Apply torque, angular motion, and radius to improve machine efficiency.

days.title: What Machines Do
days.content:
🎯 Learning Target

This week you will design, build and test a simple or compound machine and use torque, angular motion and radius to make it work better.

🔧 What a Machine Does

A machine makes a task easier in one of three ways: it multiplies force (less effort for a heavy load), changes the direction of a force (pull down to lift up), or increases speed or distance. A machine never gives you more work than you put in — if it reduces the force, you must push over a longer distance.

⚙️ The Six Simple Machines

MachineHow it helpsExample
LeverTurns around a fulcrum; long effort arm multiplies forceCrowbar, seesaw, wheelbarrow
Wheel and axleLarge wheel turns a small axle with more forceDoorknob, steering wheel
PulleyChanges direction; several pulleys reduce effortFlagpole, well bucket
Inclined planeLess force over a longer distanceRamp, mountain road
WedgeConcentrates force on a thin edge to splitBolo, axe, nail tip
ScrewAn inclined plane wrapped around a rodBolt, jar lid, jack screw

A compound machine combines two or more of these: scissors (two levers + wedges), a bicycle (wheels and axles, levers, a chain drive), a wheelbarrow (lever + wheel and axle).

✅ Quick Check

3 questions — read each explanation.

scenario.text: A bolo is used to split a coconut husk. Which simple machine is the blade?

choices.label: Wedge
Lever
Pulley
Screw

scenario.explanation: A blade is a wedge: its thin edge concentrates the force on a small area so it can split the material.

scenario.text: Which simple machine lets you pull DOWN on a rope to raise a flag UP?

choices.label: A single fixed pulley
A short inclined plane
A wedge-shaped wooden block
A long screw with fine threads

scenario.explanation: A fixed pulley at the top of the pole changes the direction of your force. It does not reduce the force, but pulling down is easier.

scenario.text: Why is a pair of scissors called a compound machine?

choices.label: It combines two levers and two wedges
It is made of metal and also plastic
It can cut many kinds of material
It has a screw that holds the blades

scenario.explanation: Each handle-and-blade is a lever turning about the pivot, and each blade edge is a wedge. Two or more simple machines working together make a compound machine.

days.title: Mechanical Advantage and Efficiency
days.content:
📐 Mechanical Advantage (MA)

MA = output force ÷ input force

If you push with 50 N on a jack and it lifts with 400 N, the MA is 400 ÷ 50 = 8. MA greater than 1 means the machine multiplies force. A single fixed pulley has MA = 1 — it only changes direction.

⚡ Efficiency

Friction wastes part of the input work as heat and sound, so useful output work is always less than input work.

efficiency = (output work ÷ input work) × 100%

Example: you do 500 J of work on a pulley system and it lifts a load by doing 400 J of work. Efficiency = 400 ÷ 500 × 100% = 80%. The missing 100 J became heat from friction.

🛠️ Raising Efficiency

  • Oil or grease moving parts (less friction).
  • Use ball bearings in wheels and fans.
  • Use lighter moving parts so less work goes into lifting the machine itself.
💡 No machine is 100% efficient — some friction is always present.

🔗 Activity 1 — Match the Pairs

Match each term to its meaning or example. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

match.why: It tells how many times the machine multiplies your force.
The load you move is bigger than the effort you apply.
It makes lifting easier by letting you pull down, not by reducing force.
It shows how much of your work becomes useful work.

match.right: Turns part of the work into heat
match.why: That is why output work is always less than input work.
Rolling balls replace sliding contact, so less energy is wasted.

match.right: Two or more simple machines together
match.why: A bicycle uses wheels and axles, levers and a chain drive.

match.right: Inclined plane wrapped around a rod
match.why: Turning it moves it forward a short distance with a large force.

days.title: Torque, Radius and Better Machines
days.content:
🔄 Torque

Machines that turn — wrenches, doorknobs, steering wheels, gears — depend on torque, the turning effect of a force:

torque (τ) = force × lever arm (r), in newton-meters (N·m)

The lever arm is the distance from the axis to where the force acts. Doubling the lever arm doubles the torque for the same effort.

🛞 Wheel and Axle

A steering wheel has a big radius; the shaft it turns has a small one. A small force at the rim makes a large torque, which turns the shaft with a large force. Tricycle and bus drivers rely on this.

⚙️ Gears

Linked gears trade speed for force. A small gear driving a big gear: the big gear turns slower but with more torque (good for climbing hills). A big gear driving a small gear: faster but weaker (good for speed on flat roads).

Example: a 40-tooth front gear drives a 20-tooth rear gear. Each pedal turn makes the rear gear turn 2 times (40 ÷ 20).

🎯 Activity 2 — Scenario Challenge

Use torque and radius to decide what works best. Read every explanation. You need 70%; retakes are unlimited.

scenario.text: A mechanic pushes a wrench with 50 N at 0.30 m from the bolt. What torque does she apply?

choices.label: 15 N·m

scenario.explanation: τ = F × r = 50 N × 0.30 m = 15 N·m. The other answers come from dividing or adding the numbers.

scenario.text: A bolt needs 60 N·m of torque to loosen. Lito can push with only 200 N. What is the SHORTEST wrench (lever arm) that will work?
scenario.explanation: r = τ ÷ F = 60 ÷ 200 = 0.30 m. A shorter wrench gives too little torque; 3.3 m is from dividing the wrong way.

scenario.text: A cyclist is about to climb a steep hill. Which gear setting makes pedaling EASIER?

choices.label: Small front gear with a large rear gear
Large front gear with a small rear gear
Same-sized front and rear gears always
Any setting, since gears do not change effort

scenario.explanation: A small gear driving a large gear makes the wheel turn slower but with more torque, so each pedal push needs less force — ideal for climbing.

scenario.text: A team tests two pulley systems lifting the same 300 N load. System A needs 150 N of effort; System B needs 100 N. Which conclusion is BEST?

choices.label: B has the greater mechanical advantage
A has the greater mechanical advantage
Both systems have the same advantage
B must be the more efficient system

scenario.explanation: MA = 300 ÷ 150 = 2 for A and 300 ÷ 100 = 3 for B. A larger MA does not by itself prove higher efficiency — that needs the work in and work out.

scenario.text: A rusty doorknob is very hard to turn. Which change would help MOST?

choices.label: Replace it with a long lever-type handle
Replace it with a smaller round knob
Paint the knob with a smooth new color
Push on the door instead of turning it

scenario.explanation: A lever handle puts your hand farther from the axis, so the same force makes more torque. A smaller knob makes it even harder.

days.title: Design, Build, Test, Improve
days.content:
🧪 Designing a Machine Like an Engineer

  1. Define the problem — e.g., "Lift a 5 kg bucket of water to the second floor with as little effort as possible."
  2. Plan — choose a machine (pulley system, lever, ramp, wheel and axle) and sketch it with measurements.
  3. Build — use safe, cheap materials: bamboo, empty spools, string, plywood.
  4. Test — measure the input force (spring scale or bathroom scale) and the load. Compute MA and, if you can measure distances, efficiency.
  5. Improve — change one thing at a time (longer lever arm, more pulleys, oiled axle) and test again.

📝 Example Test Record

VersionEffortLoadMA
1 fixed pulley50 N50 N1
2-pulley block27 N50 N1.9
2-pulley, oiled25 N50 N2.0

Changing one variable at a time lets you tell which change caused the improvement — this is a fair test.

🔐 Formative Check — Escape the Lab

3 lives, 6 keys. You need 70% (5 of 6). Read each explanation.

escape.text: A machine gives an output force of 600 N when you apply 150 N. What is its mechanical advantage?
escape.explanation: MA = output ÷ input = 600 ÷ 150 = 4. 0.25 is the inverse, 450 is the difference, 750 is the sum.

escape.text: A pulley system needs 800 J of input work and does 600 J of useful work. What is its efficiency?
escape.explanation: Efficiency = 600 ÷ 800 × 100% = 75%. Efficiency can never be more than 100%, so 133% is impossible.

escape.text: Which change will MOST likely increase the efficiency of a squeaky wheel-and-axle?

choices.label: Oil the axle to reduce friction
Paint the wheel a brighter color
Use a thicker and heavier axle
Turn the wheel more quickly

escape.explanation: Efficiency drops when friction turns work into heat and sound. Oiling the axle reduces that friction.

escape.text: Students test three lever designs but change the load AND the arm length at the same time. What is wrong with their test?

choices.label: They cannot tell which change caused the result
Levers cannot be tested in a classroom
They should have used a pulley instead
Nothing — changing two things is faster

escape.explanation: In a fair test you change one variable at a time. Changing two at once makes it impossible to know which one made the difference.

escape.text: Why can't a machine have an efficiency of 100%?

choices.label: Some energy is always lost to friction
Machines always create extra energy
The load always gets heavier with use
Mechanical advantage is always below 1

escape.explanation: Moving parts always rub, turning some of the input energy into heat and sound. Machines never create energy.

escape.text: A steering wheel with a large radius turns a thin steering shaft. Why is this design helpful?

choices.label: A small force at the rim makes a large torque
It makes the steering shaft spin much faster
It reduces the weight of the whole vehicle
It changes the direction of the vehicle's force

escape.explanation: Torque = force × radius. The large radius lets a small hand force produce enough torque to turn the shaft and the wheels.
